title: Lending Recall Prioritizer
description: Deterministic recall-queue ranking over caller-declared synthetic inputs. Ranks declared recalls by due date ascending, then declared quantity ascending, then declared id ascending (a deterministic total order), and flags a recall urgent when its due date is 0 or 1 day after the caller-declared as_of date (due-within-one-day); past-due and further-out recalls are ranked but never flagged. Dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates differenced with pure integer civil-day arithmetic -- no Date object, no runtime clock. No securities-lending tape, no borrow list, no cutoff feed, no register, no network.

as_of.description: Declared as-of date, YYYY-MM-DD; urgency is measured from this date, never from the clock.

recalls.description: Declared recalls, at most 512 entries, each with a non-empty id, a valid due date (YYYY-MM-DD), and a positive whole-number qty.

queue.description: Recall ids ranked by due date, then qty, then id; null on the fail-closed path.

urgent.description: Ids of recalls due 0 or 1 day after as_of, in queue order; null on the fail-closed path.

trace.description: Urgency clauses plus the ranking statement, or the fail-closed reasons naming each rejected input.

overall.description: QUEUE_RANKED on success, INPUT_REFUSED on the fail-closed path.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_lending_recall_prioritizer
mcp_tool_definition.description: Ranks a caller-declared recall queue by due date then declared size (then id), and flags recalls due within one day of the declared as_of date. Prioritizer over caller-declared synthetic inputs only: no securities-lending tape, no borrow list, no cutoff feed, no instruction to recall or return any security. Absent or invalid inputs are refused fail-closed and named, never silently repaired.

recalls.description: declared recalls, each with id, due (YYYY-MM-DD), and qty (positive whole number)

source: authored by RECALL-PRIORITIZER-BUILD-1 per RECALL-PRIORITIZER-BUILD-SPEC.md. Scope positioning: a prioritizer of declared inputs under named rules, not live recall data, not an instruction to recall or return any security, and not a check of any live feed; absent or invalid inputs are refused fail-closed and named, never silently repaired.
